1	"""Single-file SQL query layer.
2	
3	Public API:
4	
5	* :func:`query_file` -- run a ``SELECT ... FROM input [WHERE ...]`` query
6	  against one columnar file and return a :class:`~columnar_analytics.format.Table`
7	* :func:`query_files` -- run a statement (optionally with one equi-join)
8	  against a table-name to path mapping
9	* :func:`explain_file` / :func:`explain_files` -- parse, bind and plan the
10	  same statements without executing them; only file metadata is read
11	* :class:`QuerySyntaxError` -- lexical / grammatical errors
12	* :class:`QueryValidationError` -- unknown columns, wrong table name,
13	  type-incompatible comparisons, invalid aggregate use
14	
15	The accepted grammar (keywords case-insensitive)::
16	
17	    query       := SELECT select_item (',' select_item)*
18	                   FROM ident [WHERE expr] [GROUP BY ident (',' ident)*]
19	                   [HAVING expr]
20	                   [ORDER BY order_item (',' order_item)*]
21	                   [LIMIT uint]
22	    select_item := '*' | ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')'
23	                   | scalar_expr AS alias
24	    order_item  := (ident | agg_name '(' ('*' | ident) ')')
25	                   [ASC | DESC] [NULLS FIRST | NULLS LAST]
26	    expr       := or_expr
27	    or_expr     := and_expr (OR and_expr)*
28	    and_expr    := cmp_expr (AND cmp_expr)*
29	    cmp_expr    := not_factor (cmp_op not_factor)?
30	    not_factor  := NOT not_factor | postfix
31	    postfix     := scalar_expr (IS [NOT] NULL)?
32	    scalar_expr := term (('+' | '-') term)*
33	    term        := factor (('*' | '/') factor)*
34	    factor      := ('+' | '-') factor | atom
35	    atom        := '(' expr ')' | operand
36	                | CASE WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr
37	                  (WHEN expr THEN scalar_expr)*
38	                  (ELSE scalar_expr)? END
39	    operand     := ident | literal
40	    literal     := TRUE | FALSE | [+-]? int64 | [+-]? finite float64
41	                   | single-quoted utf8
42	
43	The supported aggregates are ``COUNT(*)``, ``COUNT(ident)`` and
44	``SUM`` / ``AVG`` / ``MIN`` / ``MAX`` applied to one column.  Without
45	GROUP BY the projection may contain aggregate expressions only; with
46	GROUP BY it may additionally contain the grouped columns.  A bare ``*``
47	must not be mixed with aggregates or grouping.  Aggregates are not
48	allowed inside WHERE, may not be nested, and aliases are not supported
49	for bare columns or aggregate calls.
50	
51	Scalar arithmetic (parentheses, unary ``+``/``-``, binary ``+`` ``-``
52	``*`` ``/``; precedence: parentheses, unary, ``*``/``/``, ``+``/``-``)
53	is available over int64 / float64 columns and numeric literals in SELECT
54	and WHERE.  A computed SELECT expression must be named with ``AS`` (the
55	alias follows the usual identifier rules and must be unique among the
56	output names); bare columns and aggregate calls keep their existing
57	result names.  int64 ``+``/``-``/``*`` on two int64 operands yields
58	int64; any float64 operand or a division yields float64, and unary
59	operators preserve the operand type.  Any NULL operand makes the result
60	NULL; the output column is nullable iff a participating column is
61	nullable (pure constants are not).  int64 overflow, division by zero and
62	non-finite float64 results raise :class:`QueryValidationError`.  A
63	numeric expression used directly as a boolean condition is rejected with
64	:class:`QueryValidationError` as well.  Non-aggregate queries execute
65	WHERE, then compute the sort keys, stably sort, apply LIMIT and only
66	then evaluate the SELECT expressions, so filtered or truncated rows
67	never trigger division-by-zero or overflow in the projection.  ORDER BY
68	may name a SELECT alias (an alias shadows an input column of the same
69	name) and sorts on the expression's result type with the usual NULL
70	placement and stability rules.  Aggregate queries do not accept scalar
71	expressions: GROUP BY keys and aggregate arguments stay plain column
72	references, and mixing a scalar expression into an aggregate query
73	raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
74	
75	Searched CASE expressions
76	(``CASE WHEN cond THEN result [WHEN ...] [ELSE result] END``; the simple
77	``CASE value WHEN ...`` form is not supported and at least one WHEN is
78	required) are scalar operands and may be nested inside more arithmetic,
79	comparisons and other CASE expressions.  For each row the WHEN conditions
80	are tested in written order and only TRUE matches; FALSE and UNKNOWN fall
81	through, an explicit ELSE supplies the fallback and a missing ELSE yields
82	NULL.  Only the chosen result is evaluated, so division by zero, int64
83	overflow or a non-finite float64 inside an unhit branch never raises; a
84	chosen result that errors still raises :class:`QueryValidationError`.
85	Every reachable THEN and an explicit ELSE must share one type family:
86	int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64, while bool and utf8 must
87	match each other exactly (any other mix raises
88	:class:`QueryValidationError`).  The result column is nullable if any
89	reachable result is nullable or the ELSE is omitted.  WHEN conditions use
90	the same boolean type check and three-valued logic as WHERE; CASE stays a
91	scalar expression, so it is rejected in aggregate arguments, GROUP BY and
92	the projection of an aggregate query just like the other scalar
93	expressions.
94	
95	Operator precedence (highest first) is NOT, comparison, AND, OR; IS [NOT]
96	NULL is a postfix of its scalar operand.  Comparison operands may be
97	column references, literals or scalar arithmetic expressions.  WHERE
98	follows SQL three-valued logic: a normal
99	comparison against NULL yields UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN propagates through the
100	logical operators, and only TRUE rows are returned.
101	
102	After WHERE, rows are grouped in GROUP BY column order (a NULL key forms
103	its own group); without an explicit ORDER BY groups come out in the order
104	of their first selected row.  An optional HAVING clause between GROUP BY
105	and ORDER BY filters the formed groups with the same boolean expression
106	grammar and three-valued logic as WHERE: its conditions combine grouping
107	columns, aggregate calls and type-compatible literals with NOT / AND / OR
108	/ comparisons / IS [NOT] NULL, only groups whose condition is TRUE are
109	kept, and aggregates named in HAVING need not appear in SELECT.  Without
110	GROUP BY HAVING filters the single global aggregate row (still produced
111	when WHERE selected no rows); with GROUP BY an empty selection yields
112	zero groups.  HAVING may not name ungrouped plain columns, ``*``, CASE,
113	scalar arithmetic or nested aggregates; it is rejected on a completely
114	non-aggregate query.  ORDER BY may only name a selected result; ASC is the
115	default, NULLs sort last regardless of direction unless NULLS FIRST /
116	NULLS LAST is given, and groups equal on every sort key keep that
117	first-row order.  LIMIT then keeps the first N groups.  Without GROUP BY
118	and aggregates an aggregate query over zero selected rows still yields one
119	output row (COUNT 0, the other aggregates NULL), unless HAVING removes it;
120	with GROUP BY it yields zero rows.
121	
122	Two-file queries (:func:`query_files`) add one equi-join to the grammar::
123	
124	    query := SELECT ... FROM left_table [join_kind JOIN right_table
125	             ON left_table.column = right_table.column] ...
126	    join_kind := INNER | LEFT
127	
128	``sources`` maps table names to file paths; only the tables referenced by
129	the statement are read.  Aliases, compound ON conditions, other join types
130	and a second join are rejected as syntax errors before any file is opened.
131	In a join query every column reference outside ``COUNT(*)`` must be
132	qualified as ``table.column`` (either part may be a double-quoted
133	identifier).  ``SELECT *`` emits the left schema followed by the right
134	schema with ``table.column`` names; explicit projections keep their
135	qualified names and aggregates keep the uppercase ``FUNC(table.column)``
136	labels.  Join keys may share a type or mix int64 with float64; NULL keys
137	never match.  INNER JOIN emits every matching combination, LEFT JOIN also
138	emits unmatched left rows with the right-side values set to NULL (the
139	right result columns are nullable).  Rows expand in left-file order, and
140	within one left row in right-file order, before WHERE / GROUP BY / HAVING
141	/ ORDER BY / LIMIT apply with their usual semantics.
142	"""
143

229	    \d+(?:\.\d*)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?   # 1, 1., 1.5, 1e3, 1.5e-2
230	    | \.\d+(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?         # .5

238	def _tokenize(sql: str) -> list[_Token]:
239	    if not isinstance(sql, str):
240	        raise QuerySyntaxError("SQL statement must be a string")
241	    tokens: list[_Token] = []
242	    i = 0
243	    n = len(sql)
244	    while i < n:
245	        ch = sql[i]
246	        if ch.isspace():
247	            i += 1
248	            continue
249	        if ch == "*":
250	            tokens.append(_Token("star", None, ch))
251	            i += 1
252	            continue
253	        if ch in ",()+-/":
254	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
255	            i += 1
256	            continue
257	        if ch in "=<>!":
258	            if ch == "!" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
259	                tokens.append(_Token("op", "!=", "!="))
260	                i += 2
261	                continue
262	            if ch in "<>" and i + 1 < n and sql[i + 1] == "=":
263	                op = ch + "="
264	                tokens.append(_Token("op", op, op))
265	                i += 2
266	                continue
267	            if ch in "=<>":
268	                tokens.append(_Token("op", ch, ch))
269	                i += 1
270	                continue
271	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character '!' at position {i}")
272	        if ch == "'":
273	            value, new_i = _tokenize_string(sql, i)
274	            tokens.append(_Token("string", value, sql[i:new_i]))
275	            i = new_i
276	            continue
277	        if ch == '"':
278	            value, new_i = _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql, i)
279	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(value, quoted=True))
280	            i = new_i
281	            continue
282	        if ch.isdigit() or ch == ".":
283	            match = _NUMBER_RE.match(sql, i)
284	            if match:
285	                text = match.group(0)
286	                tokens.append(_Token("number", _parse_number(text), text))
287	                i = match.end()
288	                continue
289	            # A '.' that does not start a number is the qualifier separator
290	            # used by two-table queries ("table.column").
291	            tokens.append(_Token("op", ".", ch))
292	            i += 1
293	            continue
294	        match = _IDENT_RE.match(sql, i)
295	        if match:
296	            text = match.group(0)
297	            tokens.append(_token_from_word(text, quoted=False))
298	            i = match.end()
299	            continue
300	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected character {ch!r} at position {i}")
301	    tokens.append(_Token("eof", None, ""))
302	    return tokens
303	
304	
305	def _token_from_word(word: str, *, quoted: bool) -> _Token:
306	    lowered = word.lower()
307	    if not quoted and lowered in _KEYWORDS:
308	        if lowered == "true":
309	            return _Token("number", True, word)
310	        if lowered == "false":
311	            return _Token("number", False, word)
312	        return _Token("keyword", lowered, word)
313	    return _Token("qident" if quoted else "ident", word, word)
314	
315	
316	def _tokenize_string(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
317	    parts: list[str] = []
318	    i = start + 1
319	    n = len(sql)
320	    while True:
321	        j = sql.find("'", i)
322	        if j == -1:
323	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated string literal")
324	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
325	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == "'":
326	            parts.append("'")
327	            i = j + 2
328	            continue
329	        value = "".join(parts)
330	        try:
331	            value.encode("utf-8")
332	        except UnicodeEncodeError:
333	            raise QuerySyntaxError("string literal is not valid UTF-8") from None
334	        return value, j + 1
335	
336	
337	def _tokenize_quoted_ident(sql: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, int]:
338	    parts: list[str] = []
339	    i = start + 1
340	    n = len(sql)
341	    while True:
342	        j = sql.find('"', i)
343	        if j == -1:
344	            raise QuerySyntaxError("unterminated quoted identifier")
345	        parts.append(sql[i:j])
346	        if j + 1 < n and sql[j + 1] == '"':
347	            parts.append('"')
348	            i = j + 2
349	            continue
350	        value = "".join(parts)
351	        if not value:
352	            raise QuerySyntaxError("quoted identifier must not be empty")
353	        return value, j + 1
354	
355	
356	def _parse_number(text: str) -> int | float:
357	    try:
358	        if any(ch in text for ch in ".eE"):
359	            value: int | float = float(text)
360	        else:
361	            value = int(text, 10)
362	    except ValueError:
363	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"invalid numeric literal {text!r}") from None
364	    if isinstance(value, int):
365	        # The magnitude 2**63 is accepted unsigned; the signed range check
366	        # happens after the optional leading sign is applied.
367	        if not (0 <= value <= 2**63):
368	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"integer literal {text} is outside the int64 range")
369	        return value
370	    if not math.isfinite(value):
371	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"float literal {text} must be finite")
372	    return value

375	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
376	# Parsed expression tree
377	#
378	# Node tuples:
379	#   ("literal", python_value, type_name)
380	#   ("column", name, table|None, table_quoted)        -- as parsed
381	#   ("column", name, index, type_name, nullable)      -- after binding
382	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node)              -- as parsed (+ - * /)
383	#   ("arith", op, left_node, right_node, type_name)   -- after binding
384	#   ("unary", operand, negate)                        -- as parsed
385	#   ("unary", operand, negate, type_name)             -- after binding
386	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None)   -- as parsed
387	#   ("case", ((cond, result), ...), else_node|None, type_name) -- after binding
388	#   ("cmp", op, left_node, right_node)
389	#   ("isnull", operand, negate)
390	#   ("not", operand)
391	#   ("and"|"or", left, right)
392	# Predicate nodes are boolean-typed (three-valued at evaluation time);
393	# "literal"/"column"/"arith"/"unary" nodes are value nodes.
394	#
395	# Projection / ORDER BY reference items:
396	#   ("column_ref", name)                 -- a plain column name
397	#   ("agg", func_upper, arg_name|None)   -- an aggregate call; arg None = '*'
398	#   ("expr", alias)                      -- a computed scalar expression
399	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
400	
401	
402	@dataclass(frozen=True)
403	class _RefItem:
404	    """One projection element or ORDER BY key as parsed."""
405	
406	    kind: str  # "star" | "column" | "agg" | "expr"
407	    name: str | None = None  # column name, or the AS alias for kind == "expr"
408	    func: str | None = None  # uppercase function name for kind == "agg"
409	    arg: str | None = None  # aggregate column argument; "" stands for '*'
410	    expr: tuple | None = None  # parsed scalar expression for kind == "expr"
411	    descending: bool = False
412	    nulls_first: bool | None = None  # None -> default (NULLs last)
413	    # Table qualifiers (two-table queries only; None when unqualified):
414	    table: str | None = None
415	    table_quoted: bool = False
416	    arg_table: str | None = None
417	    arg_table_quoted: bool = False
418	
419	
420	@dataclass(frozen=True)
421	class _Join:
422	    """The single optional equi-join of a two-table query."""
423	
424	    kind: str  # "inner" | "left"
425	    table: str  # right table name as spelled
426	    table_quoted: bool
427	    left_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
428	    right_key: tuple  # (table, table_quoted, column)
429	
430	
431	@dataclass
432	class _Select:
433	    items: tuple[_RefItem, ...]  # projection; may be a single ("star",) item
434	    table: str
435	    table_quoted: bool
436	    where: tuple | None
437	    # GROUP BY entries are (table|None, table_quoted, name) triples.
438	    group_by: tuple[tuple, ...] | None
439	    # Post-grouping boolean expression (aggregate queries only); None absent.
440	    having: tuple | None
441	    order_by: tuple[_RefItem, ...] | None
442	    limit: int | None
443	    join: _Join | None = None
444	
445	    @property
446	    def star(self) -> bool:
447	        return len(self.items) == 1 and self.items[0].kind == "star"
448	
449	    @property
450	    def has_aggregate(self) -> bool:
451	        return any(item.kind == "agg" for item in self.items)
452	
453	    @property
454	    def is_aggregate_query(self) -> bool:
455	        return self.has_aggregate or self.group_by is not None or self.having is not None
456	
457	
458	class _Parser:
459	    _CMP_OPS = frozenset(("=", "!=", "<", "<=", ">", ">="))
460	
461	    def __init__(self, tokens: list[_Token], allow_join: bool = False):
462	        self.tokens = tokens
463	        self.pos = 0
464	        # Two-table statements (qualified names + one JOIN clause) are only
465	        # enabled for query_files; single-file entry points keep rejecting
466	        # them as syntax errors.
467	        self._allow_join = allow_join
468	
469	    def parse(self) -> _Select:
470	        select = self._parse_select()
471	        if self._peek().kind != "eof":
472	            tok = self._peek()
473	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unexpected trailing input {tok.text!r}")
474	        return select
475	
476	    def _parse_select(self) -> _Select:
477	        self._expect_keyword("select")
478	        items = tuple(self._parse_projection())
479	        self._expect_keyword("from")
480	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
481	        join = None
482	        if self._allow_join:
483	            if self._accept_keyword("inner"):
484	                self._expect_keyword("join")
485	                join = self._parse_join("inner")
486	            elif self._accept_keyword("left"):
487	                self._expect_keyword("join")
488	                join = self._parse_join("left")
489	        where = None
490	        if self._accept_keyword("where"):
491	            where = self._parse_or()
492	        group_by = None
493	        if self._accept_keyword("group"):
494	            self._expect_keyword("by")
495	            names = [self._parse_group_name()]
496	            while self._accept_op(","):
497	                names.append(self._parse_group_name())
498	            group_by = tuple(names)
499	        having = None
500	        if self._accept_keyword("having"):
501	            having = self._parse_having_or()
502	        order_by = None
503	        if self._accept_keyword("order"):
504	            self._expect_keyword("by")
505	            order_items = [self._parse_order_item()]
506	            while self._accept_op(","):
507	                order_items.append(self._parse_order_item())
508	            order_by = tuple(order_items)
509	        limit = None
510	        if self._accept_keyword("limit"):
511	            limit = self._parse_limit()
512	        return _Select(
513	            items=items,
514	            table=table_tok.value,
515	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
516	            where=where,
517	            group_by=group_by,
518	            having=having,
519	            order_by=order_by,
520	            limit=limit,
521	            join=join,
522	        )
523	
524	    def _parse_join(self, kind: str) -> _Join:
525	        table_tok = self._expect_table_name()
526	        self._expect_keyword("on")
527	        left_key = self._parse_on_key()
528	        self._expect_op("=")
529	        right_key = self._parse_on_key()
530	        return _Join(
531	            kind=kind,
532	            table=table_tok.value,
533	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
534	            left_key=left_key,
535	            right_key=right_key,
536	        )
537	
538	    def _parse_on_key(self) -> tuple:
539	        tok = self._peek()
540	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
541	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
542	                f"ON requires table-qualified columns, got {tok.text!r}"
543	            )
544	        self._next()
545	        if not self._accept_op("."):
546	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
547	                "ON requires table-qualified columns (table.column)"
548	            )
549	        nxt = self._peek()
550	        if nxt.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
551	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
552	                f"expected column name after '.' in ON, got {nxt.text!r}"
553	            )
554	        self._next()
555	        return (tok.value, tok.kind == "qident", nxt.value)
556	
557	    def _parse_projection(self) -> list[_RefItem]:
558	        items = [self._parse_select_item()]
559	        while self._accept_op(","):
560	            items.append(self._parse_select_item())
561	        # Aliases are only supported for computed scalar expressions (which
562	        # consume their own "AS alias" in _parse_select_item); a trailing
563	        # identifier (including the spelling "as") where FROM is expected
564	        # names one on a bare column or aggregate.  Plain queries keep their
565	        # historical QuerySyntaxError classification; aggregate queries treat
566	        # the unsupported alias as a validation error.
567	        tok = self._peek()
568	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident") or (
569	            tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "as"
570	        ):
571	            grouped_ahead = any(
572	                t.kind == "keyword" and t.value == "group"
573	                for t in self.tokens[self.pos :]
574	            )
575	            if any(item.kind == "agg" for item in items) or grouped_ahead:
576	                raise QueryValidationError(
577	                    f"aliases are not supported; unexpected {tok.text!r} after projection item"
578	                )
579	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected FROM, got {tok.text!r}")
580	        return items
581	
582	    def _parse_select_item(self) -> _RefItem:
583	        tok = self._peek()
584	        if tok.kind == "star":
585	            self._next()
586	            return _RefItem("star")
587	        if (
588	            tok.kind == "ident"
589	            and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
590	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].kind == "op"
591	            and self.tokens[self.pos + 1].value == "("
592	        ):
593	            item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
594	            if self._arith_op_ahead():
595	                raise QueryValidationError(
596	                    "aggregate calls cannot be combined with scalar arithmetic"
597	                )
598	            return item
599	        node = self._parse_arith()
600	        if node[0] == "column":
601	            # A bare (possibly parenthesised) column reference keeps its
602	            # existing projection behaviour and needs no alias.
603	            return _RefItem(
604	                "column", name=node[1], table=node[2], table_quoted=node[3]
605	            )
606	        # A computed scalar expression must be named with AS.
607	        self._expect_keyword("as")
608	        alias = self._peek()
609	        if alias.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
610	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
611	                f"AS requires a result name, got {alias.text!r}"
612	            )
613	        self._next()
614	        return _RefItem("expr", name=alias.value, expr=node)
615	
616	    def _arith_op_ahead(self) -> bool:
617	        tok = self._peek()
618	        return tok.kind == "star" or (
619	            tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-", "/")
620	        )
621	
622	    def _parse_order_item(self) -> _RefItem:
623	        item = self._parse_column_or_agg()
624	        descending = False
625	        if self._accept_keyword("asc"):
626	            descending = False
627	        elif self._accept_keyword("desc"):
628	            descending = True
629	        nulls_first: bool | None = None
630	        if self._accept_keyword("nulls"):
631	            if self._accept_keyword("first"):
632	                nulls_first = True
633	            elif self._accept_keyword("last"):
634	                nulls_first = False
635	            else:
636	                tok = self._peek()
637	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
638	                    f"expected FIRST or LAST after NULLS, got {tok.text!r}"
639	                )
640	        return _RefItem(
641	            item.kind,
642	            name=item.name,
643	            func=item.func,
644	            arg=item.arg,
645	            descending=descending,
646	            nulls_first=nulls_first,
647	            table=item.table,
648	            table_quoted=item.table_quoted,
649	            arg_table=item.arg_table,
650	            arg_table_quoted=item.arg_table_quoted,
651	        )
652	
653	    def _qualifier_ahead(self) -> bool:
654	        nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
655	        return nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "."
656	
657	    def _parse_qualified_column(self) -> _RefItem:
658	        # Current token starts "table.column"; consumes all three tokens.
659	        table_tok = self._next()
660	        self._expect_op(".")
661	        name_tok = self._peek()
662	        if name_tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
663	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
664	                f"expected identifier after '.', got {name_tok.text!r}"
665	            )
666	        self._next()
667	        return _RefItem(
668	            "column",
669	            name=name_tok.value,
670	            table=table_tok.value,
671	            table_quoted=table_tok.kind == "qident",
672	        )
673	
674	    def _parse_column_or_agg(self) -> _RefItem:
675	        tok = self._peek()
676	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
677	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
678	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
679	            return self._parse_qualified_column()
680	        # A quoted identifier, or a bare word not spelled like an aggregate,
681	        # can only be a plain column reference.
682	        if tok.kind == "qident" or tok.value.lower() not in _AGG_NAMES:
683	            self._next()
684	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
685	        func = tok.value.lower()
686	        self._next()  # consume the function name
687	        if not self._accept_op("("):
688	            # e.g. a column literally named "count" -- the name token is
689	            # already consumed, so it is a plain column reference.
690	            return _RefItem("column", name=tok.value)
691	        arg, arg_table, arg_table_quoted = self._parse_aggregate_args(func)
692	        self._expect_op(")")
693	        return _RefItem(
694	            "agg",
695	            func=func.upper(),
696	            arg=arg,
697	            arg_table=arg_table,
698	            arg_table_quoted=arg_table_quoted,
699	        )
700	
701	    def _parse_aggregate_args(self, func: str) -> tuple:
702	        # Exactly one argument: '*' for COUNT, otherwise one (possibly
703	        # table-qualified) identifier.  Returns (name, table, table_quoted);
704	        # name "" stands for '*'.
705	        tok = self._peek()
706	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
707	            raise QueryValidationError(
708	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not a CASE expression"
709	            )
710	        if tok.kind == "star":
711	            if func != "count":
712	                raise QuerySyntaxError(f"{func.upper()} does not accept '*'")
713	            self._next()
714	            return ("", None, False)
715	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
716	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
717	                f"{func.upper()} requires one column argument, got {tok.text!r}"
718	            )
719	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
720	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
721	            nxt = self._peek()
722	            if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
723	                raise QuerySyntaxError(
724	                    f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
725	                )
726	            self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
727	            return (item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
728	        self._next()
729	        nxt = self._peek()
730	        if nxt.kind == "op" and nxt.value == "(":
731	            if tok.kind == "ident" and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES:
732	                raise QueryValidationError(
733	                    f"aggregate functions must not be nested: "
734	                    f"{func.upper()}({tok.value.upper()}(...))"
735	                )
736	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
737	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column name, not a function call"
738	            )
739	        self._reject_expression_in_agg_arg(func)
740	        return (tok.value, None, False)
741	
742	    def _reject_expression_in_agg_arg(self, func: str) -> None:
743	        # Aggregate arguments stay limited to plain column references; a
744	        # scalar expression inside an aggregate query is a validation error.
745	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
746	            raise QueryValidationError(
747	                f"{func.upper()} argument must be a column reference, not an expression"
748	            )
749	
750	    def _parse_limit(self) -> int:
751	        tok = self._peek()
752	        if (
753	            tok.kind != "number"
754	            or isinstance(tok.value, bool)
755	            or not isinstance(tok.value, int)
756	        ):
757	            raise QuerySyntaxError("LIMIT requires an unsigned integer literal")
758	        self._next()
759	        if not (0 <= tok.value <= 2**63 - 1):
760	            raise QuerySyntaxError(
761	                f"LIMIT value {tok.value} is outside the allowed range"
762	            )
763	        return tok.value
764	
765	    def _expect_table_name(self) -> _Token:
766	        tok = self._peek()
767	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
768	            return self._next()
769	        raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected table name, got {tok.text!r}")
770	
771	    def _parse_group_name(self) -> tuple:
772	        # Returns a (table|None, table_quoted, name) triple.
773	        tok = self._peek()
774	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == "case":
775	            raise QueryValidationError(
776	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not CASE expressions"
777	            )
778	        if tok.kind not in ("ident", "qident"):
779	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected identifier, got {tok.text!r}")
780	        if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
781	            item = self._parse_qualified_column()
782	            result = (item.table, item.table_quoted, item.name)
783	        else:
784	            self._next()
785	            result = (None, False, tok.value)
786	        # GROUP BY keeps accepting column references only; a scalar
787	        # expression in an aggregate query is a validation error.
788	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
789	            raise QueryValidationError(
790	                "GROUP BY only accepts column references, not expressions"
791	            )
792	        return result
793	
794	    # HAVING expression grammar ------------------------------------------------
795	    #
796	    # HAVING shares the WHERE boolean structure (NOT / AND / OR / comparison /
797	    # IS [NOT] NULL, parentheses, typed literals) but its value operands are
798	    # restricted to grouping columns, aggregate calls and literals; CASE,
799	    # scalar arithmetic and nested aggregates are rejected.
800	
801	    def _parse_having_or(self) -> tuple:
802	        node = self._parse_having_and()
803	        while self._accept_keyword("or"):
804	            node = ("or", node, self._parse_having_and())
805	        return node
806	
807	    def _parse_having_and(self) -> tuple:
808	        node = self._parse_having_comparison()
809	        while self._accept_keyword("and"):
810	            node = ("and", node, self._parse_having_comparison())
811	        return node
812	
813	    def _parse_having_comparison(self) -> tuple:
814	        left = self._parse_having_not_factor()
815	        tok = self._peek()
816	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in self._CMP_OPS:
817	            self._next()
818	            right = self._parse_having_not_factor()
819	            return ("cmp", tok.value, left, right)
820	        return left
821	
822	    def _parse_having_not_factor(self) -> tuple:
823	        if self._accept_keyword("not"):
824	            return ("not", self._parse_having_not_factor())
825	        return self._parse_having_postfix()
826	
827	    def _parse_having_postfix(self) -> tuple:
828	        node = self._parse_having_operand()
829	        # HAVING operands stay scalar references; arithmetic on top of a
830	        # group column or aggregate result is a validation error.
831	        if self._arith_op_ahead():
832	            raise QueryValidationError(
833	                "HAVING does not allow scalar arithmetic expressions"
834	            )
835	        if self._accept_keyword("is"):
836	            negate = self._accept_keyword("not")
837	            self._expect_keyword("null")
838	            node = ("isnull", node, negate)
839	        return node
840	
841	    def _parse_having_operand(self) -> tuple:
842	        tok = self._peek()
843	        if self._accept_op("("):
844	            node = self._parse_having_or()
845	            self._expect_op(")")
846	            return node
847	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value in ("+", "-"):
848	            # Only a signed numeric literal is accepted; unary +/- around a
849	            # column or aggregate is scalar arithmetic and stays rejected.
850	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
851	            if nxt.kind == "number" and not isinstance(nxt.value, bool):
852	                self._next()
853	                self._next()
854	                value = nxt.value
855	                if isinstance(value, int):

980	    def _parse_factor(self) -> tuple:

1032	            value = tok.value
1033	            if isinstance(value, bool):
1034	                return ("literal", value, "bool")
1035	            type_name = "int64" if isinstance(value, int) else "float64"
1036	            return ("literal", value, type_name)
1037	        if tok.kind == "string":
1038	            self._next()
1039	            return ("literal", tok.value, "utf8")
1040	        if tok.kind in ("ident", "qident"):
1041	            if self._allow_join and self._qualifier_ahead():
1042	                item = self._parse_qualified_column()
1043	                return ("column", item.name, item.table, item.table_quoted)
1044	            nxt = self.tokens[self.pos + 1]
1045	            if (
1046	                tok.kind == "ident"
1047	                and tok.value.lower() in _AGG_NAMES
1048	                and nxt.kind == "op"
1049	                and nxt.value == "("
1050	            ):
1051	                raise QueryValidationError(
1052	                    f"aggregate {tok.value.upper()}(...) is not allowed here"
1053	                )
1054	            self._next()
1055	            return ("column", tok.value, None, False)
1056	        if tok.kind == "keyword":

1060	    def _parse_case(self) -> tuple:
1061	        # A searched CASE: at least one "WHEN cond THEN result", an optional
1062	        # "ELSE result", terminated by END.  Conditions are boolean
1063	        # expressions; results are scalar (numeric, bool or utf8) and may
1064	        # themselves contain nested CASE expressions.  The simple form
1065	        # (CASE value WHEN ...) is not supported.
1066	        branches: list[tuple] = []
1067	        while True:
1068	            self._expect_keyword("when")
1069	            condition = self._parse_or()
1070	            self._expect_keyword("then")
1071	            result = self._parse_arith()
1072	            branches.append((condition, result))
1073	            tok = self._peek()

1076	        else_node = None
1077	        if self._accept_keyword("else"):

1079	        self._expect_keyword("end")

1084	    def _peek(self) -> _Token:
1085	        return self.tokens[self.pos]
1086	
1087	    def _next(self) -> _Token:
1088	        tok = self.tokens[self.pos]
1089	        self.pos += 1
1090	        return tok
1091	
1092	    def _accept(self, kind: str) -> bool:
1093	        if self._peek().kind == kind:
1094	            self.pos += 1
1095	            return True
1096	        return False
1097	
1098	    def _accept_op(self, value: str) -> bool:
1099	        tok = self._peek()
1100	        if tok.kind == "op" and tok.value == value:
1101	            self.pos += 1
1102	            return True
1103	        return False
1104	
1105	    def _accept_keyword(self, value: str) -> bool:
1106	        tok = self._peek()
1107	        if tok.kind == "keyword" and tok.value == value:
1108	            self.pos += 1
1109	            return True
1110	        return False
1111	
1112	    def _expect_keyword(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1113	        tok = self._peek()
1114	        if tok.kind != "keyword" or tok.value != value:
1115	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value.upper()}, got {tok.text!r}")

1117	
1118	    def _expect_op(self, value: str) -> _Token:
1119	        tok = self._peek()
1120	        if tok.kind != "op" or tok.value != value:
1121	            raise QuerySyntaxError(f"expected {value!r}, got {tok.text!r}")
1122	        return self._next()

1762	def _unify_case_types(types: list[str]) -> str:
1763	    """Unify the static types of every reachable CASE result.
1764	
1765	    int64 and float64 may mix and unify to float64; bool and utf8 must
1766	    match every other result exactly.  Anything else is incompatible.
1767	    """
1768	    unique = set(types)
1769	    if unique <= {"int64", "float64"}:
1770	        return "float64" if "float64" in unique else "int64"
1771	    if len(unique) == 1:
1772	        return next(iter(unique))

1775	        + ", ".join(sorted(unique))

1779	def _expr_type(node: tuple) -> str:
1780	    """The static type of a bound value node."""
1781	    tag = node[0]
1782	    if tag == "literal":
1783	        return node[2]
1784	    if tag == "column":
1785	        return node[3]
1786	    if tag == "unary":
1787	        return node[3]
1788	    if tag == "arith":
1789	        return node[4]
1790	    if tag == "case":
1791	        return node[3]
1792	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive

1795	def _expr_nullable(node: tuple) -> bool:
1796	    """Whether a bound value node can yield NULL (derived from its columns)."""
1797	    tag = node[0]
1798	    if tag == "literal":
1799	        return False
1800	    if tag == "column":
1801	        return node[4]
1802	    if tag == "unary":
1803	        return _expr_nullable(node[1])
1804	    if tag == "arith":
1805	        return _expr_nullable(node[2]) or _expr_nullable(node[3])
1806	    if tag == "case":
1807	        # The value is NULL only when a reachable result yields NULL, or
1808	        # every WHEN fails/UNKNOWN and no ELSE was given (implicit NULL).
1809	        # A NULL condition merely routes the row elsewhere and never makes
1810	        # a non-NULL result nullable.
1811	        if node[2] is None:
1812	            return True
1813	        return any(_expr_nullable(result) for _cond, result in node[1]) or _expr_nullable(
1814	            node[2]
1815	        )
1816	    raise QuerySyntaxError(f"unsupported expression: {tag}")  # pragma: no cover - defensive
1817	
1818	
1819	def _require_boolean(node: tuple, context: str) -> None:
1820	    if node[0] in ("cmp", "isnull", "not", "and", "or"):
1821	        return
1822	    type_name = _expr_type(node)
1823	    if type_name != "bool":
1824	        raise QueryValidationError(f"{context} requires a boolean operand, got {type_name}")
1825	
1826	
1827	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1828	# Three-valued-logic evaluation
1829	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
1830	
1831	
1832	def _eval(node: tuple, row: tuple) -> bool | None:
1833	    tag = node[0]
1834	    if tag == "literal":
1835	        return node[1]
1836	    if tag == "column":
1837	        return row[node[2]]
1838	    if tag == "unary":
1839	        value = _eval(node[1], row)
1840	        if value is None:
1841	            return None
1842	        if not node[2]:  # unary plus keeps the value
1843	            return value
1844	        return _negate_value(value)
1845	    if tag == "arith":
1846	        left = _eval(node[2], row)
1847	        right = _eval(node[3], row)
1848	        if left is None or right is None:
1849	            return None
1850	        return _arith_value(node[1], left, right)
